title: A rat model of contrast-induced acute kidney injury following intra-arterial contrast administration
author: Zhiqing Wang
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.z6bf9an
materials: Body weight of each rat was measure.

steps.title: Deprive rats of water
steps.instruction: Withhold water from each rat for 48 hours prior to any surgical manipulation.

steps.title: Induce deep anesthesia
steps.instruction: Inject pentobarbital sodium intraperitoneally at 40 mg kg⁻¹ to achieve deep anesthesia.

steps.title: Cannulate femoral vein and carotid artery
steps.instruction: Insert short peripheral catheters (24 G × 21 mm) into the right femoral vein and right carotid artery.

steps.title: Collect baseline blood sample
steps.instruction: Draw 1 mL of arterial blood from the carotid catheter for baseline serum creatinine (SCr) determination.

steps.title: Prepare and inject indomethacin
steps.instruction: Dissolve indomethacin in phosphate buffer (pH 8.4) to 5 mg mL⁻¹ and administer intravenously at 10 mg kg⁻¹.

steps.title: Inject L‑NAME after 15 min
steps.instruction: Fifteen minutes after indomethacin, inject L‑NAME dissolved in 0.9 % normal saline (10 mg mL⁻¹) intravenously at 10 mg kg⁻¹.

steps.title: Administer contrast or control
steps.instruction: Fifteen minutes after L‑NAME, randomize rats to receive either iopromide (contrast‑induced AKI group) or normal saline (control) via the carotid catheter at 7.8 mL kg⁻¹ infused over 5 minutes.

steps.title: Allow postoperative recovery
steps.instruction: Place each rat in an individual cage with free access to tap water and standard chow.

steps.title: Re‑anesthetize at 12 h
steps.instruction: Twelve hours after contrast injection, re‑induce deep anesthesia with pentobarbital sodium 40 mg kg⁻¹ i.p.

steps.title: Collect second arterial blood
steps.instruction: Obtain a second arterial blood sample from the ventral aorta for later analysis.

steps.title: Perfuse kidneys with saline
steps.instruction: Perfuse both kidneys through the bilateral renal arteries with 0.9 % normal saline to remove blood cells.

steps.title: Harvest and fix kidneys
steps.instruction: Excise both kidneys, bisect longitudinally, and fix the right kidney (cortex + medulla) in 10 % neutral‑formal­in liquid for histology.

steps.title: Euthanize with overdose pentobarbital
steps.instruction: Euthanize each rat by intraperitoneal injection of pentobarbital sodium 200 mg kg⁻¹.

steps.title: Centrifuge blood samples
steps.instruction: Within 2 hours of collection, centrifuge blood at 1000 × g for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Measure serum creatinine
steps.instruction: Determine SCr concentrations at the hospital clinical laboratory using a standard method.

steps.title: Process kidney tissue for histology
steps.instruction: Prepare kidney sections for H&E staining.

substeps.instruction: Embed kidneys in paraffin and cut 3–4 µm thick sections.
Deparaffinize slides with xylene three times, 2 min each.
Rehydrate through ethanol series: 100 % ethanol three times, 1 min each; 80 % ethanol 1 min; then rinse in distilled water.
Stain nuclei with hematoxylin: incubate 4 min, rinse tap water 2 min.
Dip slides in 0.1 % hydrochloric acid in alcohol for 30 s, rinse 1 min.
Dip in 0.5 % ammonia solution for 1 min (background turns light blue), rinse 1 min.
Stain cytoplasm with 1 % eosin for 50 s, rinse tap water.
Dehydrate with 100 % ethanol three times, 1 min each, then clear in xylene three times, 1 min each.
Mount slides with resinous mounting medium and store at room temperature.

steps.title: Examine stained slides
steps.instruction: View H&E‑stained kidney sections under a light microscope.

steps.title: Grade tubular injury
steps.instruction: Assess tubular injury using the Paller score: examine 100 tubules from 10 high‑magnification (×200) fields of the medulla and outer medulla per kidney and assign a semi‑quantitative score.
